text: A new microservice, agents-matrix-connector: its own public repo and submodule (orchestrator step O1), one image with migrate, api and a singleton bot, its own database, on agents-common with the agents-orchestrator session names.

It connects to the existing Matrix deployment as the plain bot user @agents:szymonrichert.pl with an access token, like Hermes; no appservice and no Synapse configuration change beyond creating the account (user-run U1, U2).

Users talk to agents through Facebook via the existing mautrix-meta bridge, with the bot logged in to the bridge with its own Facebook account (user-run U3, U4 if needed); encrypted rooms are marked and never answered.

Users, chats and rooms are auto-discovered: invites are joined, rooms classified (dm, group, matrix, infrastructure), members and Facebook ids recorded, and only text messages taken in, without replaying history.
There is an allowlist and a denylist over Matrix user id, Facebook id, room id and alias (display name deny only); deny wins and the default is deny.

Each chat maps to one agents-orchestrator session from its preset, reused while it runs, falling back to a new one when gone; the agent's final text of each turn is posted back to the chat exactly once, with typing while it works.

A UI API under /matrix/api/v1 and a Chats page in agents-web show discovered rooms and users with their decisions and recent messages, and edit the rules, room presets and triggers and the default preset.
Headless parity (README API, openapi.json, API e2e against fakes) and a live deploy into namespace agents through agents-helmfile with a green smoke that never sends a chat message.
